# Kalasha Award for Best Lead Actor in a Film

| holder_label = Most recent winner
| holder = Godwill Odhiambo, Where the River Divides (2024)

| website =
}}
The Kalasha Award for Best Lead Actor in a Film is an annual award presented by the Kenya Film Commission as part of the Kalasha International Film & TV Awards. It recognizes an actor who has delivered an outstanding performance in a leading role in a Kenyan film.
First awarded at the inaugural ceremony in 2009, the category is considered one of the most prestigious acting honors in the Kenyan film industry.
The recent recipient is Godwill Odhiambo for his performance in Where the River Divides at the 13th edition held in 2024.
Criteria
The award is presented to an actor in a leading role whose performance demonstrates exceptional artistic merit, emotional depth, and contribution to the narrative of a film. Eligible performances must appear in films submitted to the Kenya Film Commission during the awards cycle and meet the official entry requirements.
Nominees and winners are selected by the Kalasha Academy, a panel of industry professionals including directors, producers, actors, and technical experts. In general categories, the outcome is determined through a hybrid voting system, where the academy contributes 70% of the vote and the public accounts for 30%.
Winners
The award ceremony was not held in 2013, 2016, 2023, and 2025. Winners are listed by year of ceremony.

Records
As of 2024, several actors have received multiple nominations in this category, reflecting sustained excellence in leading roles. However, comprehensive records of multiple wins and nominations are still being documented as the awards continue to expand.
Most nominations
The record for the most nominations in the category is currently a five-way tie, with each of the following actors having received two nominations:
* Peter King Mwania – 2 nominations (2009, 2014)
* Maina Olwenya – 2 nominations (2014, 2017)
* Elsaphan Njora – 2 nominations (2017, 2026)
* Brian Ogola – 2 nominations (2018, 2019)
* Joe Kinyua – 2 nominations (2019, 2026)
